questions.q: In this course, what is a "business process"?
options: A repeatable sequence of steps where one action triggers the next until work is done
Any Apex trigger that fires on save
A report that tracks revenue over time
A Salesforce object's page layout
questions.explain: A business process is a repeatable sequence of steps, like submit, approve, reimburse, that organizations ran long before any software enforced it.

questions.q: Which tool blocks a record from being saved outright when data doesn't meet a standard?
options: Email Alerts
Validation Rules
Approval Processes
Reports
questions.explain: Validation Rules evaluate a formula and block the save, with an error message, when the formula returns true.

questions.q: What does "clicks before code" mean as a working default for admins?
options: Apex should never be used in any Salesforce org
Prefer declarative tools like validation rules and Flow before reaching for custom code, when they can do the job
Always build the UI before writing any formulas
Validation rules must be written before approval processes
questions.explain: It's a maintainability and speed argument: configuration doesn't need a deploy pipeline and survives upgrades more reliably, though some requirements genuinely need code.

questions.q: Which running example does this chapter use to tie the lessons together?
options: A case escalation process for Support
A hiring and onboarding process for new employees
A discount approval process for Opportunities
A lead assignment process for Marketing
questions.explain: The chapter builds one discount approval process for Opportunities piece by piece: a validation rule, an approval process, and an email alert.

questions.q: Which tool tells a human it's their turn to act in a process?
options: Formulas
Validation Rules
Page Layouts
Email Alerts
questions.explain: Email Alerts (and the notification templates approval processes use) are what actually tell a person a process needs their attention.
